server.Ohne Stopp: Läuft der Server, schickt Ha: Without a stop: if the server is running, Hatchtower sends this command to the console and waits briefly so the game finishes writing its save – nobody gets kicked. Examples: Minecraft “save-all”, Terraria “save”. Games without a console command (e.g. Satisfactory, Enshrouded) save on their own regularly; leave it empty then. Only someone with “Send commands” may set it; anyone with the right to run the job may then run it.

server.Hier stehen zwei verschiedene Arten von: There are two different kinds of backups here: those Hatchtower creates with its backup jobs and stores on your backup target, and those {panel} creates itself and keeps on its side. Both can be downloaded here.
server.Diese Backups legt Hatchtower mit seinen: Hatchtower creates these backups with its backup jobs and stores them on the backup target (drive or network share). Each is a fixed state from a certain point in time – that is why they can be downloaded and restored to the server.
server.Diese Backups hat {panel} selbst angeleg: {panel} created these backups itself – by hand in the panel or with its own schedules. They are kept where {panel} stores backups (usually on the Wings server), not by Hatchtower. Such a backup always contains the whole server. Hatchtower shows them and downloads them for you; creating, restoring and deleting is done in the panel.
server.{server}: Backups im Panel nicht lesbar: {server}: backups in the panel cannot be read – {grund}
server.Im Panel gesperrt: wird von dessen Aufbe: Locked in the panel: its retention does not delete it.
server.Wird über Hatchtower aus dem Panel gelad: Downloaded from the panel through Hatchtower.
server.{panel} hat für deine Server noch keine: {panel} has not created any backups for your servers yet.
server.Dazu kommen die Backups, die {panel} sel: On top of that come the backups {panel} creates itself: they are listed in their own section under “Stored backups” and can be downloaded there. They are kept by the panel, not by Hatchtower.
server.Dieses Backup gibt es im Panel nicht (me: This backup does not exist in the panel (any more).
server.Hinweis: Hatchtower läuft hier über http: Note: Hatchtower runs over http:// without encryption here. That is why browsers warn on every download (“insecure download”) – the file is fine, you can keep it. With HTTPS, e.g. through a reverse proxy, the warning goes away.
server.Bei {n} Backup(s) fehlt die Datei auf de: For {n} backup(s) the file is missing on the Wings node: {panel} still lists them, but they can be downloaded neither here nor in the panel. Common causes: Wings runs in Docker and the backup folder (/var/lib/pterodactyl/backups) is not mounted as a volume, so the files are lost when the container is recreated; the folder was cleaned up; or the Wings config.yml has a different backup_directory. You can delete such entries in the panel.
server.Falls die Datei inzwischen wieder da ist: In case the file is back by now
server.Die Datei zu „{backup}“ fehlt auf dem Wi: The file of “{backup}” is missing on the Wings node – {panel} still lists the backup, but the file is gone. It is now marked in the list.
server.Läuft Hatchtower zu Hause, geht jeder Do: If Hatchtower runs at home, every download to the outside (e.g. a backup) goes through the upload of your internet line. With a limit the line stays usable, even while someone downloads a large backup. It applies to all downloads together.
server.Im eigenen Netz nicht begrenzen: Do not limit within the own network
server.Vor Hatchtower sitzt ein Reverse-Proxy,: A reverse proxy sits in front of Hatchtower but is not entered above. Every visitor then looks like the proxy and the limit does not work properly – please enter its IP above.
